newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Koor jumps amid off-the-floor purchases.
newsitem.headline: Koor jumps amid off-the-floor purchases.

text.p: Koor Industries shares were up 5.25 percent at 387.77 shekels at midsession on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange amid rumours of further off-the-floor purchases on Monday, traders said.

The bourse said 257,000 shares were sold off the floor on Sunday, a block equal to nearly two percent of Koor's equity. This included two large blocks -- one for 93,000 shares and another for 150,000 shares -- purchased at 415 shekels a share, a 15 percent premium to the market price.
The other shares were sold in smaller blocks at 368.43 shekels, the same as Sunday's closing price.
All together about $30 million in shares were sold.
A source close to the deal said Bank Hapoalim provident funds had sold $11 million worth of shares on Sunday.
Provident funds managed by Bank Leumi sold the other large block of shares, traders said.
Israeli newspapers said a foreign investor was behind the purchases.
"I heard Bank Leumi, the bank, not its provident funds, was buying the shares," a trader said. The trader did not know if the purchases were for the bank's nostro account or for a client.
A spokeswoman for Bank Leumi said she could not comment on the reports, and a Koor spokesman declined to comment.
Koor chairman Stanley Gold has expressed disappointment in the share's lacklustre performance and has proposed spinning off the company's biggest publicly traded subsidiaries to shareholders.
But at least one other major foreign shareholder has said he thinks the shares are underpriced.
Gold is president of Koor's second-biggest shareholder Shamrock Holdings Ltd, the investment vehicle of the Roy Disney family, which controls about 20 percent of Koor.

Koor's biggest shareholder, Hapoalim, has not commented on the proposal but bank officials said they would not act on it until Hapoalim itself was sold. The bank is in the process of being privatised.
Koor, Israel's largest holding company, is also traded on the New York Stock Exchange.
-Tova Cohen, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 TCC DER
